definition: Approximating an intractable posterior with a simpler distribution by maximizing the evidence lower bound.
details: Approximating an intractable posterior with a simpler distribution by maximizing the evidence lower bound. The objective behind VAEs and the mathematical scaffolding from which diffusion model training objectives were originally derived.

explainer.lead: Variational inference approximates an intractable posterior with a simpler distribution by maximizing the evidence lower bound. It matters as the objective behind VAEs and the mathematical scaffolding from which diffusion model training objectives were originally derived.

tiers.eli5: When the exact answer is too hard to compute, you pick a simpler stand-in and tune it until it fits as well as possible.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers optimize the ELBO as a stand-in for the true posterior, which is the objective behind VAEs. The pitfall is that maximizing a bound does not guarantee the approximation matches the true posterior closely.
tiers.paperLevel: Approximate an intractable posterior with a simpler distribution by maximizing the evidence lower bound. Limits: the ELBO is a bound, so its value does not by itself certify approximation quality.

explainer.example: A VAE is trained by maximizing the ELBO over its encoder and decoder, using the bound in place of the intractable data likelihood.
